method: Grouped by where each case is in its news cycle, not by guilt. Dates and statuses were re-checked Nov. 18 to 20, and all ten entries again on Nov. 25 against court coverage and our sourced court calendar. The outlets that reported each update are named in its card; where a date comes from fewer than three independent sources it is marked reported.

phases.label: Building up
phases.blurb: A big court moment is coming. Attention usually grows for weeks beforehand, longest before a trial.

phases.label: In the spotlight now
phases.blurb: A major moment just happened or is happening. Attention tends to peak for about a week.

phases.label: Past the peak
phases.blurb: The big moment has passed. Attention usually falls to a small fraction of its peak within one to four weeks, unless a new court date arrives.

cases.title: Maggie and Paul Murdaugh: Alex Murdaugh's retrial
cases.status: AWAITING RETRIAL · DISMISSAL MOTION DENIED NOV. 20 · RETRIAL SET FOR APRIL 5, 2027
cases.why: His 2023 murder convictions were overturned in May 2026. On Nov. 20, 2026, Judge Debra McCaslin denied his motion to dismiss the murder indictments, the Associated Press, ABC News and FITSNews reported. The retrial is set for April 5, 2027 in Sumter County, a date that can change. He is presumed innocent of the murder charges.

cases.title: The Lindsay Clancy case
cases.status: MISTRIAL · APPEAL BEFORE FULL SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT · PAUSE DENIED (REPORTED NOV. 25) · RETRIAL STILL SET MARCH 29, 2027
cases.why: Her trial ended in a mistrial on Sept. 4, 2026, which is not a verdict. On Nov. 19, a justice of the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court sent her double jeopardy petition to the full court, with arguments expected in January 2027. That referral is not a ruling. By Nov. 25, the court had denied prosecutors' request to pause the retrial while the appeal is heard, without giving a reason, Boston 25 News and Fox News reported. The retrial is still set for March 29, 2027, and a status hearing for Dec. 30. She has pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent.

cases.title: The Susan Smith parole hearing
cases.status: PAROLE DENIED NOV. 19 · MAY APPLY AGAIN IN 2028
cases.why: South Carolina's parole board voted unanimously on Nov. 19, 2026 to deny parole to Susan Smith, who was convicted of murder in 1995 for the deaths of her two sons, SC Daily Gazette, NBC News and FOX Carolina reported. Their father, David Smith, asked the board to keep her in prison. NBC News reports she can ask again in 2028.

cases.title: The Richard Glossip case
cases.why: On Nov. 12, 2026, Oklahoma prosecutors dropped the first-degree murder charge and Richard Glossip pleaded guilty to a lesser charge in the 1997 death of Barry Van Treese, the Associated Press reported. The attorney general's office calls it accessory to murder; his defense calls it accessory after the fact. He has not been sentenced. The Death Penalty Information Center reports sentencing on Dec. 17; the AP says only December, and one outlet says Dec. 17 and 18.

cases.title: The Palisades Fire case: Jonathan Rinderknecht
cases.status: FOUND GUILTY NOV. 20 · SENTENCING SET FOR MARCH 17, 2027
cases.why: A federal jury in Los Angeles found Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Nov. 20, 2026 of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce, ABC7, NBC Los Angeles and UPI reported. Prosecutors said he started the fire that grew into the January 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people. His first trial ended in a mistrial in June, with jurors split 10 to 2 for acquittal. He has not been sentenced; sentencing is set for March 17, 2027. A conviction can be challenged on appeal.

cases.title: The Dwain Hall case
cases.status: FOUND GUILTY NOV. 20 · TWO CONSECUTIVE LIFE TERMS (REPORTED)
cases.why: A Marion County, Florida jury found Dwain Hall guilty of first-degree murder and kidnapping in the death of Sonia Exelby on Nov. 20, 2026, and he was sentenced to two consecutive life terms, the State Attorney's Office and Court TV reported. A conviction can be challenged on appeal.

cases.title: The Tomasz Kosowski case
cases.why: Judge Joseph Bulone sentenced Tomasz Kosowski to death on Nov. 20, 2026 for the first-degree murder of Steven Cozzi in Pinellas County, Florida, CNN, ABC News and FOX 13 reported. Bulone found him guilty on Sept. 23 after a bench trial in which Kosowski represented himself. The sentence can be challenged on appeal.

cases.title: The Naresh Bhatt case
cases.status: CONVICTED NOV. 10 · SENTENCING SET FOR MARCH 12, 2027
cases.why: A Prince William County, Virginia, jury found Naresh Bhatt guilty on all counts on Nov. 10, 2026, in the death of his wife, Mamta Kafle Bhatt, FOX 5 DC, WJLA and CNN reported. Sentencing is scheduled for March 12, 2027.

cases.title: The Idaho student murders: the Bryan Kohberger case
cases.why: Kaylee Goncalves, Madison Mogen, Xana Kernodle and Ethan Chapin were killed in 2022. Kohberger pleaded guilty and was sentenced to four consecutive life terms in July 2025. In July 2026 he filed a petition for post-conviction relief, which ABC News and NBC News reported. We have not seen a ruling on it.

cases.title: The Jared Bridegan case
cases.why: Judge London Kite sentenced Mario Fernandez Saldana on Nov. 12, 2026 to life in prison for first-degree murder, plus 30 years for solicitation, to run concurrent with the life term, the State Attorney’s Office announced. A jury found him guilty on Aug. 26 of first-degree murder and solicitation to commit a capital felony in the killing of Jared Bridegan. Shanna Gardner and Henry Tenon are charged and presumed innocent; their trial is set for 2027.
